**VERDICT: REVISE** **Overall Assessment**: The carousel implements basic interactive controls and dynamic `alt` text, but fails to communicate state changes to assistive technology, lacks required landmark/region labeling, and omits keyboard navigation patterns mandated by the WAI-ARIA Carousel pattern. The design relies on visual-only feedback for active indicators and assumes dynamic `alt` text triggers screen reader announcements (it does not). These are structural design gaps that will cause complete functional loss for screen reader users and significant friction for keyboard users. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: Before reading the code, I predicted: (1) missing `aria-live` region for dynamic image updates, (2) visual-only active state on indicators lacking `aria-pressed`, (3) unlabeled carousel container missing landmark/region semantics, and (4) absence of arrow key navigation per APG Carousel pattern. All four predictions were confirmed during investigation. **Critical Findings** (blocks access): 1. **Dynamic `alt` text does not trigger assistive technology announcements; no `aria-live` region exists.** - Evidence: `src/components/BuggyCarousel.jsx:16` (`alt={`Carousel image ${currentIndex + 1}`} />`) and absence of any live region in the component tree. - User group impacted: Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver). - WCAG/APG citation: WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages), WAI-ARIA Carousel Pattern (requires `aria-live="polite"` for dynamic content updates). - Why this matters: Screen readers do not announce changes to the `alt` attribute on an existing `` element. When users click Previous/Next, the image visually changes but the screen reader hears nothing. The core functionality is invisible. - Fix: Add a visually hidden region that updates with the carousel state: `
Image {currentIndex + 1} of {images.length}
`. Alternatively, use `role="status"` on an existing container and update its text content synchronously with index changes. **Major Findings** (significantly degrades experience): 1. **Indicator buttons lack programmatic active state (`aria-pressed`).** - Evidence: `src/components/BuggyCarousel.jsx:25` (`className={idx === currentIndex ? 'active' : ''}`) - User group impacted: Screen reader users, keyboard-only users. - WCAG/APG citation: WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), WAI-ARIA Carousel Pattern (indicators must use `aria-pressed="true/false"`). - Why this matters: Active state is communicated only via CSS class `.active`. Screen readers cannot determine which indicator corresponds to the current slide.
